tag: Episode 52S · Letters Through an Open Door
title: Letters Through an Open Door

beats.t: On their first morning in the world of fortune, Yeoni switched off all three alarms and fell asleep again in a little room among the World Tree's roots.
Get up. What happens to your dignity if the person who chose this world is late on their very first day?
Doesn't the person who saved the world get a pass on wake-up calls?
No. There is an apple for breakfast, though. Get up now and I'll make you tea.
Yeoni's eyes flew open. The little kettle smelled of lotus blossoms, and Moka's saucepan beat drifted in through the window.
Tap, tap, tapping, wake the morning air. Fry the five elements, fill it with flair!
The whole rapping-otter-chef concept finally makes perfect sense.
From that day on, Yeoni took charge of a small consultation table at the Destiny Teahouse. It was a place to help people find their own sentences, rather than hand them answers.
Your heart seems to be running ahead, while the other person's pace is a little slower. Instead of pressing for reassurance, what if you leave room for a breath?
The wind fairy having the consultation stopped crying and nodded. Yeoni poured another cup of tea.
You left room for choices without making pronouncements. That was a good consultation.
Of course. I chose my own destiny. I can't go closing off somebody else's ending.
That evening, the golden line of the twenty-third door opened. Beyond it appeared Yeoni's studio apartment in reality and Seo Hanbi's yellow umbrella.
Yeoni, can you hear me? I'll read you the letter your mother sent.
The letter's first line was brief. Wherever you are, are you eating properly? At the second line, the ink had lingered a long time.
It hurts that you're gone, but you say you chose where to live, so I'm going to try to trust you. Take good care of your heart there, too.
I'll write back to Mom. I'll tell her I'm still oversleeping, working, and sharing meals with good people here.
And write that I take care of your socks.
Leave that out. You'll make it sound like I can't even put socks on without you.
I can hear both of you perfectly. Byeongha, no more hiding your name.
Park Byeongha. Neo. Yeongnyangi. Every name Yeoni calls me is mine. I'm not letting go of a single one now.
When the letter ended, the golden line did not close. It became a little star. Yeoni hung it by the teahouse window.
Send them some otter rap, too. Let's see if people in reality know a decent beat.
As long as this door exists, the two worlds aren't cut off. But the place where you make your life is here now, Yeoni.
Yes. I didn't stay because I couldn't go back. I chose a life here, with a door through which I can send news.
That night, Yeoni and Byeongha walked among the World Tree's roots. Lights glowed in the small houses beneath them, and far away the river of the moon shimmered.
Yeoni. Let's build a house, too. Not too far from the teahouse, and a little farther from Moka's morning beat.
All right. Big windows. Space for two umbrellas. And no sock inspection checklist on the fridge.
Byeongha smiled. Yeoni took his hand. Cool metal and warm wood walked at the same pace.

The first month at the teahouse passed very slowly. Every day, Yeoni organized the consultation notes and revised the words for the next person, making them a little easier to understand than yesterday.
Yeoni's consultations were not prophecies. They were closer to showing the flow of the five elements and shedding light together on the paths a person could choose within it.
Having a lot of Water energy doesn't always make someone gentle. When there's too much, your feelings may have trouble finding somewhere to flow. Today, let's make one small vessel for them.
At the back of the teahouse, Byeongha repaired and rehung a broken door handle and an old wind-chime mirror. With every nail he drove, Yeoni promised another star in his review.
Fixing one door handle is harder than being a customer service agent. Still, this is about building a home that will stay, not memories to erase.
At dinner, Moka's cooking always occupied the center of the table. It tasted different every day, was usually good, and occasionally left everyone drinking nothing but water.
You can't back up a failed dish, either. So you remember today's flavor and stir-fry tomorrow to a different beat.
Don't justify bad food by comparing cooking to destiny.
Yet Yeoni did not dislike what he had said. They were all already learning how to use an irreversible day as an ingredient for the next, instead of throwing it away.
When the second letter arrived from reality, Seo Hanbi's handwriting was neater than in the first. She wrote that she was learning a new job in a school counseling office.
I used to think even an apology was a debt. Now I'm learning that the person you become after apologizing matters more.
Hanbi, that was a good choice. But don't start trying to bear everything alone. Open the door and talk when things get hard.
Yeoni decided that they might rescue someone, but would not take on all that person's burdens. Making a place to carry them together offered comfort that lasted longer.
You've learned how to respect someone's choices. Then respect mine, too.
What is it? If you've secretly made another dangerous plan on your own, it doesn't count.
Let's prepare to get married. Sign the papers, make our promises in front of everyone, and turn this house into an address that belongs to us both.
Yeoni covered their mouth. Their eyes widened in surprise, and then a color like the purple ribbon spread across both cheeks.
Was that a proposal? Who starts a proposal with paperwork and an address?
Apparently, I do. And if you'd like, I can do it again.
Do it again. But the answer will be the same. Let's live together, Park Byeongha. Neo. Yeongnyangi.
The words were almost too characteristically Byeongha to be called a proposal, but Yeoni understood: he would never abandon his name or his address again.
Before writing their wedding vows, they wrote down the expressions each wore when frightened. Love was less an ability to read minds than a habit of asking and waiting.
If you don't understand my expression, ask instead of guessing. Even in a world of divination, I'll speak for my own heart.
That is the hardest promise, and the most necessary. I'll keep it.
[ A Moonlit Homesite · A New Promise Between Two People ]
